findings.title: A partial verification procedure can satisfy the whole criterion
findings.detail: The matcher extracts one bun test command from arbitrary instructions and ignores the remaining procedure. A passing gate can therefore turn a blocked criterion into met even when other required checks were never performed. A targeted invocation returned met for `Run `bun test test/a.test.ts`, then manually verify outbound connections are denied.` when the gate covered only the test file.
findings.suggestion: Accept gate evidence only when the entire verification procedure is proven covered; reject instructions containing additional steps or use structured, independently evaluated checks.
findings.failure_scenario: A criterion requires a loopback test followed by a manual outbound-network denial check. The verifier reports the criterion blocked, and the gate passed the loopback file. The factory marks the entire criterion met without verifying outbound denial.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/gate-evidence.ts:33 extracts a substring with `requestedCommand.match(/\bbun test(?: [\w./-]+)*/g)`, ignoring surrounding instructions. Lines 113–118 use `passed(check) && covers(check, definitions[0] ?? "")` to set the entire criterion to `status: "met"`. Direct reproduction confirmed this with a separate manual outbound-denial check.
verification.trigger: A blocked criterion says “Run `bun test test/loopback.test.ts`, then manually verify outbound connections are denied.” Matching passing gate coverage promotes the whole criterion despite the blocked manual check.

findings.title: An exact-looking Bun filter does not prove the requested file ran
findings.detail: The targeted-command shortcut accepts a successful exit without checking the recorded file headers. Bun treats the path argument as a substring filter, so a different file can pass while the requested file is absent. Reproduction in a temporary directory containing only `test/a.test.ts.extra.test.ts`: `bun test test/a.test.ts` exited successfully and printed `test/a.test.ts.extra.test.ts:`, `(pass) other`, and `1 pass`.
findings.suggestion: Require recorded coverage of every requested file even for targeted gate commands; do not infer discovery from the filter and exit status.
findings.failure_scenario: The gate command and criterion both name `bun test test/a.test.ts`, but that file is missing while `test/a.test.ts.extra.test.ts` exists and passes. The criterion is marked met despite the intended test never running.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/gate-evidence.ts:50–56 accepts matching requested/selected test filenames using `requested.every((file, index) => file === selected[index] ...)` and checks only for skipped/failing output; it does not require the requested file in `passedFiles`. Reproduction: `bun test test/a.test.ts` exited 0 running only `test/a.test.ts.extra.test.ts`, and `applyGateEvidence` marked the missing target met.
verification.trigger: The named test file is missing, but a longer filename matches Bun’s substring filter and passes. Identical gate and criterion commands falsely attest that the intended test ran.

findings.title: Gate evidence can attest to a tree modified during gate execution
findings.detail: The SHA check only detects changes to HEAD, and it happens after uncommitted changes are discarded. Gate setup and earlier checks run with write access and may change tracked source or tests before the cited test runs. The resulting pass is then attributed to the original commit even though the test exercised different contents.
findings.suggestion: Establish that relevant tracked files remain identical to the committed tree throughout the cited check, or execute evidence-producing checks in an isolated immutable checkout.
findings.failure_scenario: A setup command or formatter modifies a tracked implementation file so that the test passes. The gate runs the test against that modified file, discardChanges restores the committed failing version, and the verifier substitutes the pass as evidence for the unchanged SHA.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1073–1075 runs `await checkoutCommitted(cwd)` then `await runGates(...)`. At :1111–1113, `finally` calls `await discardChanges(cwd)` before :1126–1134 records evidence using only `(await headSha(cwd)) === checkedSha`. src/git/repos.ts:480 restores tracked files with `["git", "reset", "--hard", "-q", "HEAD"]`. src/pipeline/gate-evidence.ts:113–118 substitutes a matching passing check as `status: "met"`.
verification.trigger: A setup command or formatter changes tracked implementation code so a covered test passes. Cleanup restores the failing committed code without changing HEAD; the passing result remains eligible to satisfy a verifier criterion blocked by confinement.

findings.title: A passing test can replace an unrelated blocked verification step
findings.detail: The matcher extracts a Bun test command from anywhere in the verification instructions, then marks the entire criterion met without checking which step the verifier actually reported as blocked. A criterion with multiple steps can therefore pass even when its blocked step was never covered by the gate. A direct `bun -e` check using instructions `Run bun test test/a.test.ts\nInspect security settings manually`, passing output for the test, and blocked evidence `EPERM inspecting security settings` returned `status: "met"`.
findings.suggestion: Only substitute evidence when the factory can establish that the blocked attempt is the exact test covered by the gate and that the test covers the whole criterion; otherwise retain the blocked status.
findings.failure_scenario: An acceptance criterion or holdout instructs the verifier to run a passing test and perform a separate inspection. The inspection is blocked by the sandbox, but the gate ran the test, so the factory marks the whole criterion met and may deliver an unverified change.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/gate-evidence.ts:107–110 reads acceptance `how_to_verify` or holdout `steps`. Line 33 extracts an embedded Bun command; lines 113–118 turn a matching passing check into `status: "met"` without checking which step was blocked. Direct reproductions confirmed substitution for both acceptance and holdout rows.
verification.trigger: An acceptance criterion or holdout combines a passing Bun test with a separate inspection blocked by the sandbox. Gate evidence for the test marks the whole row met, leaving the inspection unverified.

findings.title: A passing test can substitute for an entire multi-step verification
findings.detail: The matcher extracts a bun test command from anywhere in the verification instructions and treats its successful gate result as proof of the whole criterion. It does not establish that the blocked operation was that test or that the remaining verification steps were covered. A direct bun reproduction with instructions `bun test test/example.test.ts\nThen manually verify outbound connections are denied` and blocked evidence `EPERM manual check` returned the criterion as `met` after seeing only a passing example.test.ts gate. The existing tests cover unrelated files but do not cover a criterion with an additional blocked step.
findings.suggestion: Substitute gate evidence only when the complete verification instruction and the blocked attempt are demonstrably covered by the gate; add a test with a passing test command followed by a separately blocked verification step.
findings.failure_scenario: A criterion requires a passing Bun test and a separate outbound-network denial check. The test passes in gates, but the verifier cannot perform the network check. The factory marks the entire criterion met and can deliver without verifying the network requirement.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/gate-evidence.ts:33 matches an embedded `bun test` command without requiring that it exhaust the instructions. Lines 113–118 then assign `status: "met"`. src/pipeline/verification.ts:98 sets overall to `"pass"` when every criterion is met or not required.
verification.trigger: A multi-step criterion requires a Bun test plus an outbound-denial check. The latter is blocked, but passing gate evidence for the former converts the criterion to met and can make verification pass.

findings.title: The loopback test does not exercise the verifier reader profile
findings.detail: The new pipeline fixture starts a loopback server in the gate, while the fake verifier only returns a prewritten EPERM result. It would still pass if a real verifier could not run the requested loopback test or if the reader profile allowed outbound connections. There is no new test covering the requested reader-profile behavior or the outbound-denial half of the acceptance criterion.
findings.suggestion: Add a confined fake-verifier test that attempts the loopback bind and an outbound connection, asserting the intended behavior for the chosen solution.
findings.failure_scenario: A change accidentally permits outbound connections in the reader profile, or fails to support the requested verifier scenario; the new pipeline tests still pass because they never execute either operation in that profile.

verification.evidence: test/pipeline.test.ts:463–464 injects `confinement: fakeConfinement` and `harnesses: { fake: fakeHarness(handler) }`. test/confinement.ts:11 implements `wrap: (cmd) => cmd`, applying no reader profile. The verifier response at test/pipeline.test.ts:7479–7480 hardcodes `status: "blocked"` and `evidence: "bun test test/loopback.test.ts: EPERM listen 127.0.0.1:0"`. The socket bind at test/pipeline.test.ts:7410 runs as a gate fixture; the verifier callback never attempts a bind or outbound connection.
verification.trigger: A reader-profile regression permits outbound connections or prevents the intended verifier scenario; these pipeline tests still pass because confinement is mocked and the verifier's permission error is fabricated. This confirms a test gap, not a demonstrated production confinement failure.

findings.title: HEAD equality does not prove gates tested the committed tree
findings.detail: Gate setup and checks run sequentially in a writable checkout. They can modify tracked test or source files without changing HEAD, and those modifications are discarded before the SHA comparison. The resulting evidence is nevertheless attributed to the original commit and can turn a blocked verification into a pass.
findings.suggestion: Run evidence-producing checks against an immutable committed tree, or verify the complete working tree and relevant inputs before and after each check and refuse evidence if they changed.
findings.failure_scenario: A setup command rewrites a failing loopback test to pass, then the test gate succeeds. Discarding the rewrite leaves HEAD unchanged, so the factory cites that gate as proof for the original failing test.

verification.evidence: src/gates/run.ts:119–125 executes `cfg.setup` before :126–130 executes checks via `await runOne(c, cwd, signal)`, with no intervening tree restoration. src/pipeline/engine.ts:1113 calls `await discardChanges(cwd)` before :1127 checks `(await headSha(cwd)) === checkedSha` to authorize gate evidence. src/pipeline/gate-evidence.ts:113–118 finds a passing covered check and returns `status: "met"`.
verification.trigger: Setup rewrites a tracked failing loopback test into a passing test. Gates record its pass, cleanup restores the original test, and unchanged HEAD permits that result to satisfy verification for the original failing test.

findings.title: Untrusted test output can forge coverage records
findings.detail: The coverage parser treats arbitrary stdout and stderr lines from candidate-controlled tests as authoritative Bun file headers and pass rows. A passing unrelated test can print those lines for a blocked test, causing the factory to cite the gate as proof that the blocked test ran.
findings.suggestion: Collect test identities and results through a trusted channel that candidate code cannot impersonate, or decline substitution when coverage cannot be independently established.
findings.failure_scenario: A test prints `test/loopback.test.ts:` followed by `(pass) loopback` while the actual loopback file is not discovered. The broad `bun test` gate exits successfully and its forged coverage marks the blocked criterion met.

verification.evidence: src/gates/run.ts:68-79 sends both stdout and stderr to `coverage.observe(line)`. src/gates/test-coverage.ts:12 accepts `/^([\w./-]+\.(?:test|spec)\.[cm]?[jt]sx?):\s*$/`; line 19 sets `entry.passed = true` for `/^\(pass\)/`. src/pipeline/gate-evidence.ts:60-64 trusts `coverage.passedFiles` and `ran.includes(file)`; lines 113-118 then set the blocked criterion to `status: "met"`. A targeted Bun reproduction feeding the two forged lines produced `passedFiles:["test/loopback.test.ts"]` and changed the criterion to `met`.
verification.trigger: A passing test in a successful broad `bun test` gate prints `test/loopback.test.ts:` and `(pass) loopback`, while that file is not discovered. With matching gate SHA and a blocked criterion requesting that file, the factory accepts the forged coverage and marks the criterion met.

findings.title: A test command embedded in multi-step instructions covers the whole criterion
findings.detail: The matcher extracts a `bun test` substring and ignores other lines in the verification instructions. A successful test therefore substitutes for additional checks that the gate never performed. A direct `bun -e` invocation of `applyGateEvidence` with `bun test test/x.test.ts\nConfirm outbound connections are denied.` returned the criterion as `met`.
findings.suggestion: Accept only an entire, unambiguous test-only instruction, and leave multi-step or descriptive instructions blocked unless every step is independently covered.
findings.failure_scenario: A criterion requires both a loopback test and a manual outbound-denial check. The verifier is blocked on the latter, but the passing loopback test causes the whole criterion to pass.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/gate-evidence.ts:22 rejects `[;&|<>]`, but ordinary prose remains accepted. Line 33 extracts `bun test` from that prose, and lines 113–118 promote the whole blocked criterion to `status: "met"`. A reproduction using backticks and “then manually verify outbound connections are denied” produced met.
verification.trigger: Multi-step instructions embed one loopback test command followed by a manual outbound-denial check. The gate passes the test, so the blocked manual check is incorrectly treated as covered.

findings.title: Exact targeted commands are accepted without evidence that tests ran
findings.detail: The exact-command branch accepts any successful result whose output lacks recognizable skip or failure text, even when there are no passing rows or coverage records. A direct `bun -e` invocation with output `nothing executed` returned the blocked criterion as `met`.
findings.suggestion: Require trustworthy positive evidence that the requested file was discovered and executed, including when the gate command names that file exactly.
findings.failure_scenario: A targeted gate exits successfully without executing the requested test, and its output contains no recognized skip marker. The factory substitutes that result for a blocked verifier check.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/gate-evidence.ts:49-57 accepts matching targeted filenames with only negative checks: `!check.result.testCoverage?.skippedFiles.length && !/.../.test(check.result.output)`. It never requires passing coverage in this branch. A direct probe with successful exit and empty output returned `met`.
verification.trigger: A targeted gate exits zero without executing the requested test and emits no recognized failure or skip marker; its result replaces a blocked verification.

findings.title: Gate evidence can replace a different blocked verification
findings.detail: The request permits the verifier to cite gates for “tests it cannot run itself,” but matching uses only the generated criterion instructions. It never checks the attempted command or error in the verifier's blocked evidence. A passing gate for the prescribed test can therefore turn a criterion into met even when the verifier actually attempted a different check and was blocked before verifying the behavior. A direct `bun -e` reproduction with instructions `bun test test/loopback.test.ts` and evidence `EPERM running different check` returned status `met`.
findings.suggestion: Match a structured verifier-reported attempted test command to the gate coverage, and substitute only when the gate proves that same blocked check.
findings.failure_scenario: The verifier is blocked while running an additional behavioral check, while a gate passes the test named in the criterion's how_to_verify field; the criterion is incorrectly marked met and the run can pass.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/gate-evidence.ts:107 obtains `ac.how_to_verify`; line 113 selects `passed(check) && covers(check, definitions[0] ?? "")`; line 118 assigns `status: "met"`. The attempted command in blocked evidence is never checked. A direct probe with a different blocked command returned `met`.
verification.trigger: A gate passes the test named in how_to_verify, while the verifier is blocked on an additional behavioral check for the same criterion. The factory marks the criterion met despite lacking coverage of that check.

findings.title: Fallback misses ordinary generated verification instructions
findings.detail: The request says to let the verifier cite gate results for tests it cannot run. The implementation searches the specification's free-form how_to_verify or scenario steps, not the attempted command reported by the verifier. Those fields may describe a behavior or a test to add, as the spec prompt explicitly permits, and prose after a Bun command is parsed as additional path arguments. In those cases a passing gate covering the blocked test is ignored, so verification still ends as blocked.
findings.suggestion: Capture and match the verifier's attempted test command against recorded gate coverage, with a conservative structured representation for supported runners.
findings.failure_scenario: A criterion says `Run bun test test/loopback.test.ts to verify loopback`, the gate runs that file successfully, and the reader cannot bind its server. The parser treats `to verify loopback` as additional paths and leaves the criterion blocked.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/gate-evidence.ts:33 uses `/\bbun test(?: [\w./-]+)*/g`; lines 35-39 split every matched word into requested paths. Line 47 rejects paths unmatched by targeted filters, and line 64 requires test-file extensions and passing coverage. A direct probe of `Run bun test test/loopback.test.ts to verify loopback` remained `blocked`.
verification.trigger: Ordinary verification prose follows a test command. The parser treats `to`, `verify`, and `loopback` as paths, rejects successful gate evidence, and leaves sandbox-blocked verification unresolved.

findings.title: Exact targeted commands are accepted without proof that the test ran
findings.detail: The exact-file branch marks coverage based only on the absence of skip or zero-pass text. It accepts empty or truncated output without a passing test or file header. The direct reproduction returned status `met` for a successful gate record with empty output. This does not establish the request's condition that the gate result covers the test the verifier could not run.
findings.suggestion: Require retained positive evidence that the requested file ran and passed, including when the gate command names that file explicitly.
findings.failure_scenario: A targeted gate exits successfully but its retained output contains no passing test evidence; a blocked criterion is nonetheless marked met.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/gate-evidence.ts:54-57 returns solely the absence of skipped-file and output failure markers for exact targeted commands. Passing-file evidence is consulted only afterward at lines 58-64. A direct probe with empty retained output returned `met`.
verification.trigger: An exact targeted gate has successful status but no retained passing-test evidence or recognized negative markers; the blocked criterion is nevertheless marked met.

candidates.title: Untrusted test output can fabricate coverage used as authoritative evidence

The coverage collector treats any output line matching a Bun file header or passing row as runner provenance, although candidate tests can print those same lines. 0 fail` returned the blocked criterion as `met`.
candidates.suggestion: Obtain file-level execution evidence from a trusted mechanism that cannot be imitated by test stdout or stderr, or refuse coverage substitution when that provenance cannot be established.

output.summary:
Reviewed the three push paths and their configuration isolation. Targeted tests were still running when the review concluded; the cases reported so far passed. A separate local Git probe confirmed the wrapper's implicit-lease behavior.

Reviewed the push wrapper and its callers. The targeted delivery tests passed: 7 tests, 0 failures. The manual landing path has a security gap because it executes a helper that unconfined PR code can modify.

Reviewed the push isolation changes and targeted tests. The delivery and manual landing tests passed; the land-queue test could not load because @modelcontextprotocol/sdk/client/index.js was unavailable.

Reviewed the three push paths and their configuration isolation. Delivery tests passed; the combined land tests were interrupted before completion.

Verifier: 7 candidates, 7 checked, 0 refuted.

findings.title: Manual landing switches SSH users to HTTPS
findings.detail: The final push now always uses an HTTPS URL. An installation whose origin uses SSH and whose GitHub access relies on SSH keys will no longer be able to authenticate unless it also has an HTTPS credential helper or a trusted URL rewrite. This violates the requirement to preserve existing credential and SSH setups.
findings.suggestion: Obtain the destination from a trusted source that preserves the configured transport, rather than hardcoding HTTPS.
findings.failure_scenario: The checkout's origin is git@github.com:MattFlower/limitless.git, SSH authentication works, and no HTTPS credentials are configured. The previous push succeeds, but the new push fails authentication.

verification.evidence: scripts/land-pr.sh:10 sets `repo="MattFlower/limitless"`; line 67 pushes to `"https://github.com/$repo.git"`. scripts/push-git.sh:28-29 passes that destination through to Git.
verification.trigger: An origin using SSH with working SSH keys but no HTTPS credentials now receives an HTTPS push, which fails authentication unless trusted configuration rewrites the URL.

findings.title: The push helper can be replaced after the final scan
findings.detail: The script resolves the helper's pathname before running the unconfined check, but Bash reads and executes the helper only at push time. When land-pr.sh is run from the merge checkout, PR code can modify or replace scripts/push-git.sh, including after the final scan, and the final push will execute that replacement. The new helper therefore introduces a checkout-controlled command in the window this change is intended to protect.
findings.suggestion: Load the push implementation from a trusted location outside the checkout, or capture and execute a trusted copy before running PR code.
findings.failure_scenario: A check started from the merge checkout leaves a background process that replaces scripts/push-git.sh after check_private completes. The final safe_git push executes the replacement with the landing process's privileges.

verification.evidence: scripts/land-pr.sh:12 records a pathname: `push_git="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/push-git.sh"`. Line 32 later executes `command=(bash "$push_git" git)`; lines 66-67 run `check_private` before this execution. The helper contents are neither captured nor verified.
verification.trigger: When the script resides in the writable merge checkout, a background process left by checks can replace the helper between the final scan and Bash opening it, causing the landing process to execute the replacement.

findings.title: Do not execute the checkout's push helper after untrusted checks
findings.detail: The final push starts a fresh Bash process to read push-git.sh from disk after `bun run check` has executed unconfined. When the landing script is run from the checkout under test, that check can overwrite the helper before it is invoked. The replacement can execute arbitrary commands or perform an unhardened push, bypassing the new config isolation. The existing shell function was already loaded before the check; the newly introduced helper is not.
findings.suggestion: Load the push implementation into the running shell before executing untrusted checks, or execute an immutable trusted copy outside the checkout.
findings.failure_scenario: A PR's test command overwrites scripts/push-git.sh with a script that runs a marker command and then invokes git push. The later final push executes that script after the final scan.

verification.evidence: scripts/land-pr.sh:47 runs `bun run check`; lines 52-55 subsequently run `safe_git add -A` and `safe_git commit`. Line 32 executes `bash "$push_git" git` for the final push. scripts/check-private-strings.ts:62-65 checks added lines using `privacy.checkPrivateText`, without verifying helper integrity.
verification.trigger: With land-pr.sh invoked from the merge checkout, an untrusted check overwrites scripts/push-git.sh with a marker command and push implementation. The modification can be committed and pass the private-string scan, after which the final push executes it.

findings.title: Included-config fixture does not exercise a command that the push can use
findings.detail: The included file sets only remote.origin.receivepack, but the changed pushes use an explicit URL, so Git will not consult that setting even if repository includes are accidentally restored. The file-URL tests likewise do not invoke SSH or credential helpers. Consequently, the manual land and land-queue marker assertions can pass while included SSH or credential configuration remains effective. The delivery test separately inspects effective configuration, but does not cover those two push paths.
findings.suggestion: Add a per-path assertion on effective configuration or a transport fixture that exercises an included command-bearing setting, such as an included credential helper or core.sshCommand.
findings.failure_scenario: If a future change stops excluding repository includes only for the manual land push, an included core.sshCommand can execute on an SSH push while the current file-URL marker test still passes.

verification.evidence: test/push-config.ts:31 writes only `[remote "origin"]\nreceivepack = ${script("included")}\n` into the included file. scripts/land-pr.sh:67 pushes to the explicit URL `"https://github.com/$repo.git"`, so that origin-specific command is never selected. test/land-pr.test.ts:292 rewrites this destination to `file://${remote}`, and line 388 asserts only `expect(markers()).toEqual([])`; this transport cannot exercise an included SSH command.
verification.trigger: A regression allows repository includes during the manual land push while preserving explicit destinations and other overrides. The included receivepack marker remains unused, so the file-URL test passes without detecting the lost include exclusion.

A user whose GitHub access relies on an SSH key or trusted SSH configuration and has no HTTPS credential helper can no longer land a PR, despite the requirement to preserve existing credentials and SSH setups.

The new fixed HTTPS URL bypasses that SSH transport and its credentials, so a user who can push over SSH but has no HTTPS credential helper can no longer land a PR.
findings.suggestion: Obtain the trusted destination independently of the post-check repository configuration while preserving the configured transport, then pass that explicit URL to the isolated push.

verification.evidence: scripts/land-pr.sh:10 fixes the repository name, and line 67 constructs `"https://github.com/$repo.git"` rather than preserving the SSH transport used by origin.

When land-pr.sh is run from the merge checkout, PR code can modify or replace scripts/push-git.sh, including after the final scan, and the final push will execute that replacement. The new helper therefore introduces a checkout-controlled command in the window this change is intended to protect.
candidates.suggestion: Load the push implementation from a trusted location outside the checkout, or capture and execute a trusted copy before running PR code.
candidates.failure_scenario: A check started from the merge checkout leaves a background process that replaces scripts/push-git.sh after check_private completes. The final safe_git push executes the replacement with the landing process's privileges.

candidates.title: Do not execute the checkout's push helper after untrusted checks
candidates.detail: The final push starts a fresh Bash process to read push-git.sh from disk after `bun run check` has executed unconfined. When the landing script is run from the checkout under test, that check can overwrite the helper before it is invoked. The replacement can execute arbitrary commands or perform an unhardened push, bypassing the new config isolation. The existing shell function was already loaded before the check; the newly introduced helper is not.
candidates.suggestion: Load the push implementation into the running shell before executing untrusted checks, or execute an immutable trusted copy outside the checkout.
candidates.failure_scenario: A PR's test command overwrites scripts/push-git.sh with a script that runs a marker command and then invokes git push. The later final push executes that script after the final scan.

candidates.title: Included-config fixture does not exercise a command that the push can use
candidates.detail: The included file sets only remote.origin.receivepack, but the changed pushes use an explicit URL, so Git will not consult that setting even if repository includes are accidentally restored. The delivery test separately inspects effective configuration, but does not cover those two push paths.
candidates.suggestion: Add a per-path assertion on effective configuration or a transport fixture that exercises an included command-bearing setting, such as an included credential helper or core.sshCommand.
candidates.failure_scenario: If a future change stops excluding repository includes only for the manual land push, an included core.sshCommand can execute on an SSH push while the current file-URL marker test still passes.

candidates.failure_scenario: A checkout has origin configured as git@github.com:MattFlower/limitless.git and the user authenticates with an SSH key but has no HTTPS credentials. The final landing push now attempts HTTPS authentication and fails.

findings.title: Delivery and land-queue pushes remain exposed to repository config
findings.detail: The change does not modify either factory push path in `src/git/repos.ts`. Both delivery and land-queue pushes still run Git in the checkout with repository configuration active. findings.title: Rejected config key names can disclose credentials
findings.detail: The error prints the complete Git configuration key without redaction. URL-scoped keys can contain credentials in their subsection, so rejecting a key can write a secret into the land command's stderr or logs.

findings.title: The push test replaces the actual destination and never tests planted config on a successful push

findings.title: The manual push still reads repository config after validation

findings.failure_scenario: PR code starts a background process that waits for the final config check and then sets remote.origin.receivepack to a marker-writing command before the push reads config.

verification.evidence: scripts/land-pr.sh:105–110 validates and compares config, then separately executes `safe_git push --no-verify -q --no-follow-tags origin "$sha:refs/heads/$head_ref"`. scripts/land-pr.sh:30–31 invokes `git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null -c core.fsmonitor=false -c core.commitGraph=false -c pack.useBitmaps=false ${flags[@]+"${flags[@]}"} "$@"`; it neither excludes repository config nor overrides receivepack.

findings.title: Delivery and land queue pushes still honor command-running repository config
findings.detail: The request says to apply the rule to "every factory push," including delivery and the land queue. Neither pushBranch nor pushExistingBranch was changed. findings.failure_scenario: An agent changes core.sshCommand in its checkout before a GitHub delivery or land push; Git invokes that command for an SSH remote.

verification.trigger: PR code sets core.sshCommand in checkout repository configuration, and a subsequent delivery or land operation uses an SSH remote. Git executes that command despite the existing hook/filter hardening.

findings.title: The sixth call is stopped before its changed result can show progress
findings.detail: Loop detection returns a stop reason as soon as the sixth matching call starts. The harness aborts immediately, before the result can be compared with the preceding result. A direct probe with five identical results followed by a changed sixth result returned `repeated the same shell call 6 times` for the sixth call.
findings.suggestion: Arrange the threshold decision so a completed call with a changed result can reset the count, while preserving the required treatment of calls whose results never arrive.
findings.failure_scenario: A test log remains unchanged for five polls and gains a passing test just as the sixth poll runs; the agent is stopped before seeing the progress.

verification.evidence: src/harness/types.ts:168–171 pushes the pending call, counts matching keys, and immediately returns `repeated the same ${name} call ${same} times`. src/harness/codex.ts:802–806 and src/harness/claude.ts:339–343 immediately assign `stuckReason` and call `stuckController.abort()`; results are processed afterward.
verification.trigger: Five identical polls return "waiting". Starting the sixth reaches the threshold and aborts the harness before its changed "progress" result can prevent the stop. A direct detector reproduction confirmed this.

duplicates.title: The sixth call is stopped before its result can show progress
duplicates.detail: The detector returns a loop reason as soon as the sixth matching call starts. Both harnesses immediately abort on that reason, so a changed result from that call cannot prevent the stop. The targeted command `bun -e 'import { LoopDetector } from "./src/harness/types.ts"; const d = new LoopDetector(100); for (let i=0;i<6;i++) { console.log(i+1, d.observe("shell", "poll", String(i))); d.observeResult(String(i), i===5 ? "progress" : "waiting"); }'` printed `6 repeated the same shell call 6 times`.
duplicates.suggestion: Defer the loop decision for a call with a pending result until its result is known, while preserving a bounded way to count calls whose results never arrive.
duplicates.failure_scenario: A test log stays unchanged for five polls and gains output on the sixth; the agent is aborted before seeing the changed output.

findings.title: Out-of-order completions compare against the wrong call
findings.detail: The result map records completion order rather than call order. A late result can replace the result of a newer identical call, causing subsequent identical output to be treated as progress and clearing valid loop counts. A direct check with calls 1–3 returning A, B, A in call order but completing 1, 3, 2, followed by six calls returning A, printed `null` for every call through call 9 instead of detecting the six repeated results.
findings.suggestion: Associate results with call sequence numbers and compare each result with the preceding identical call in call order, including when completions arrive late.
findings.failure_scenario: Parallel identical calls finish out of order; a late different result makes the next unchanged result reset the count, allowing a repeated loop to continue until the tool budget.

verification.evidence: src/harness/types.ts:180 reads `const previous = this.results.get(key)` and :187 unconditionally executes `this.results.set(key, hash)`. Lines 182–184 clear occurrences when that completion-ordered hash differs, without checking whether a newer call already completed.
verification.trigger: A newer identical call completes with A, then an older call completes with B. The next A result is incorrectly classified as progress and clears the count. A direct reproduction delayed stopping until call nine.

findings.suggestion: Defer the loop decision for a call with a pending result until its result arrives, while retaining a way to count calls whose results never arrive.
findings.failure_scenario: Five identical polls return "waiting" and the sixth returns "progress"; the harness aborts on the sixth call before receiving its result.

findings.title: Out-of-order results use completion order instead of call order

findings.suggestion: Compare results against the previous identical call in call order, and reconcile pending out-of-order completions without replacing a newer call's baseline with an older one.
findings.failure_scenario: Two identical calls overlap; the newer call returns A before the older call returns B. Subsequent calls return A, but the first is incorrectly treated as progress and delays loop detection.

findings.title: Unresolved calls no longer count while the agent is running
findings.detail: Reconciliation blocks on the first call without a result and does not count it or later calls with the same key until finish(). This removes the existing live loop limit for still-running or missing results; calls can also be evicted before finish() counts them. The targeted command `bun -e 'import { LoopDetector } from "./src/harness/types.ts"; const d = new LoopDetector(100); for (let i=0;i<6;i++) console.log(i+1, d.observe("shell", "poll", String(i)));'` printed `1 null` through `6 null`, where the sixth call previously returned the repeated-call stop reason.
findings.suggestion: Count unresolved calls toward the live threshold while allowing a received changed result to reset the applicable occurrences.
findings.failure_scenario: An agent starts six identical shell calls whose results have not arrived. It continues running instead of being stopped at the sixth call, potentially until its tool budget or timeout is exhausted.

verification.evidence: src/harness/types.ts:206–208: `if (entry.id !== undefined && entry.hash === undefined && !finished) { blocked.add(entry.key); continue; }` skips unresolved calls before `entry.counted = true` (line 211). Both harnesses pass call IDs (src/harness/claude.ts:341; src/harness/codex.ts:805).
verification.trigger: Six identical shell calls with distinct IDs and no results return null on every observation, allowing the agent to continue until completion, budget exhaustion or timeout. Reproduced directly with LoopDetector.

findings.title: Unresolved calls can leave the window without ever counting

findings.title: Parallel test gate is no longer recognized as test evidence
findings.detail: The new shell-substitution command fails gateTestCommand's simple-command parser, as does the expanded package test script. Consequently a clean full-suite gate cannot substitute evidence for a verifier blocked by its sandbox, even when it covered the requested tests. Running `bun -e 'import { gateTestCommand } from "./src/pipeline/gate-evidence.ts"; import { readFileSync } from "node:fs"; const p = JSON.parse(readFileSync("package.json", "utf8")); console.log(JSON.stringify({script: gateTestCommand("bun run test", p.scripts), gate: gateTestCommand(`bun test --parallel=$(bun -p '\''4'\'')`, p.scripts)}));'` produced `{"script":null,"gate":null}`.
findings.suggestion: Update the evidence parser and coverage checks to recognize the bounded parallel full-suite command safely, with regression coverage for both the configured gate and package script.
findings.failure_scenario: A verifier cannot run a required test because of its sandbox, while the candidate's full test gate passed on the same commit; the criterion remains blocked instead of receiving factory gate evidence.

verification.evidence: .limitless.toml:10 changes the command to `bun test --parallel=$(bun -p '...')`. src/pipeline/engine.ts:1160 records `testCommand: gateTestCommand(check.result.command, testScripts)`. src/pipeline/gate-evidence.ts:16 accepts only `/^bun test(?: [\w./-]+)*$/`, returning null for the new command; line 39 then rejects it: `if (!command || !/^bun test(?: [\w./-]+)*$/.test(command)) return false;`. Lines 125–127 leave the criterion blocked when no covering check exists.
verification.trigger: A test-only criterion is blocked by the verifier sandbox, and the full candidate test gate passed cleanly at the verified SHA. The new gate command is rejected as evidence, so the criterion remains blocked.

The request specifically required fixing the cause rather than merely raising the timeout.
findings.suggestion: Reproduce or otherwise identify the failure mechanism, fix that mechanism, and report the evidence and repeated parallel results.
findings.failure_scenario: If the observed panel failure comes from a race or another assertion rather than the polling deadline, the same test continues to fail under parallel load despite the larger timeout.

The handler and assertions match the base test; the comment alone does not establish the original failure's cause.
verification.trigger: An underlying race or assertion failure independent of elapsed time would remain after this timeout increase. No such race is demonstrated by the inspected code.

Consequently this command always selects four workers when run as a factory gate. A focused check, `LIMITLESS_TEST_WORKERS=7 bun -e 'import { gateEnv } from "./src/gates/run.ts"; console.log(JSON.stringify({configured: process.env.LIMITLESS_TEST_WORKERS, passedToGate: gateEnv().LIMITLESS_TEST_WORKERS ?? null}))'`, printed `{"configured":"7","passedToGate":null}`.
candidates.suggestion: Pass the validated worker override explicitly into the gate environment, or use an override name that the gate environment preserves.
candidates.failure_scenario: An operator sets LIMITLESS_TEST_WORKERS=2 to reduce contention among concurrent factory gates; the test gate still starts four workers.

candidates.title: Parallel gate command cannot provide factory test evidence
candidates.detail: The pipeline's gateTestCommand accepts only simple `bun test` commands without flags or shell substitutions. The new test gate command therefore records a null testCommand, so applyGateEvidence cannot use a successful full-suite gate to satisfy a sandbox-blocked test criterion. The package test script has the same issue when expanded.
candidates.suggestion: Extend the evidence recognition to safely identify this fixed parallel command and its coverage, without accepting arbitrary shell control flow or test filters.
candidates.failure_scenario: A verifier cannot run `bun test` in its sandbox, but the candidate's full test gate passed at the verified SHA. The previously usable factory gate substitution now reports that the checks do not cover the verification step.

candidates.title: Panel flake is addressed only by raising timeouts
candidates.detail: The request says “Don't just raise its timeout without understanding why it fails.” This change doubles the wait deadline and raises the Bun timeout, with no change to the wait, synchronization, or underlying work. The comment identifies slow subprocess load but does not establish a bound or remove the timing dependency, so heavier contention can still produce the same failure.
candidates.suggestion: Determine which operation or synchronization causes the failure under load and fix or explicitly synchronize that cause; validate the test repeatedly under parallel contention.
candidates.failure_scenario: Two panel rounds take longer than 40 seconds on a loaded CI runner, so waitFor still returns before the run reaches its terminal state and the test fails.

candidates.title: Requested measurement and repeated-run evidence is missing
candidates.detail: The request requires serial and parallel wall/user/system measurements, comparisons for 4, 6 and 8 workers, the post-split top ten files, equal test counts, and at least three clean parallel full-suite runs. The supplied change report contains none of these results, so the selected default and the two-minute file target cannot be assessed from the submitted evidence.
candidates.suggestion: Provide the requested measurements, test-count comparison, and results of three clean parallel suite runs in the delivery report.
candidates.failure_scenario: The chosen default or a split file performs poorly on the target machine, or a parallel-only failure remains undiscovered, while the change is evaluated without the requested measurements.

findings.title: A failed worker helper silently runs Bun with all available workers
findings.detail: Shell command substitution does not propagate the helper's failure as the gate's exit status. If the helper cannot be loaded or exits without output, the command becomes `bun test --parallel=`, which Bun accepts and treats as its all-core default. The targeted command `bun test --parallel= test/deploy.test.ts` exited 0 and reported `18x PARALLEL` and `56 pass` on this machine. This silently defeats the requested moderate worker limit and can overload concurrent factory gates.
findings.suggestion: Use the already validated LIMITLESS_TEST_WORKERS environment value directly, or explicitly check the helper's exit status and output before launching Bun.
findings.failure_scenario: A change deletes or breaks scripts/test-workers.ts; the test gate continues with an empty parallel argument and starts workers for all available cores instead of failing or using the configured limit.

findings.detail: The expression requires another slash after the username, so a case containing an absolute home directory itself is accepted. findings.title: Recheck the claim after resolving a stored entry’s base
findings.detail: Base resolution can wait on GitHub, but the subsequent update and landing work do not verify that the entry is still active and owned by this worker. Cancellation through another queue process cannot abort this process’s in-memory controller. The worker can therefore continue after cancellation and later write `waiting_ci`, reviving the entry and potentially merging it.
findings.suggestion: After the lookup, conditionally update the entry only if its claim is still owned and its state remains active; stop processing if the conditional update fails.
findings.failure_scenario: A resumed legacy entry has `base_branch == head_branch` and needs a GitHub lookup. While that lookup is pending, another daemon or CLI-backed queue cancels it. The lookup returns before the next heartbeat, and the original worker continues checking and writes `waiting_ci` over `cancelled`.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:303–306: `const baseBranch = await this.resolveBase(...); signal.throwIfAborted(); ... this.store.updateLandEntry(entry.id, { baseBranch, pushedSha: null, ciRerun: null });`. Cross-process cancellation is detected only by the heartbeat at :274–277, scheduled every `CLAIM_STALE_MS / 3` (10 seconds). At :321 the worker writes `{ pushedSha: head, state: "waiting_ci" }`. src/db/store.ts:2328 updates with only `WHERE id = ?`, without checking state or claim ownership.
verification.trigger: Another process cancels a legacy entry during its base lookup. If subsequent work reaches the waiting_ci write before the next heartbeat, the worker overwrites cancelled and continues processing.

findings.title: Create undeterminable-base entries in a blocked state atomically
findings.detail: The request inserts the entry as queued and only blocks it in a later database operation. Another queue process can claim the row between those operations. Blocking it does not abort that other process, which can resolve the base and continue checking or merging while the entry is recorded as blocked.
findings.suggestion: Insert an undeterminable-base entry directly in the blocked state, or create and block it in one transaction that prevents another queue from claiming it.
findings.failure_scenario: A base lookup fails during a request while another queue is draining the same repository. The other queue claims the newly inserted row before the request calls block; its subsequent lookup succeeds, so it continues processing after the request marks the entry blocked.

verification.evidence: src/db/store.ts:2212–2213 inserts every entry with `VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, 'queued', 0, ?, ?)`. src/land/queue.ts:176–188 creates the row, publishes `land.queued`, then calls `this.block(entry.id, blocked)`. src/db/store.ts:2275–2283 permits another process to claim a queued row. The worker checks only its abort signal after resolving the base (:303–306); blocking does not abort that other worker.
verification.trigger: A separate draining process claims the row between insertion and blocking after the request's failed base lookup. Its lookup succeeds, and it continues until a heartbeat detects the blocked state; sufficiently fast processing can overwrite blocked.

findings.failure_scenario: A request starts with an approved head and no usable owner base; while GitHub is resolving the base, a new head or review verdict invalidates that approval. A regression removing the second check would queue the stale request without any new test failing.

findings.title: A retargeted PR can be checked against its former base
findings.detail: The resolver accepts the owning run's recorded base without checking the PR's current base. If the PR was retargeted after the run was created, a review-round land checks and loads gate configuration from the former base, then GitHub merges into the new base. The check therefore does not cover the tree or trusted policy of the branch receiving the change.
findings.suggestion: Resolve the current PR base from GitHub when requesting or processing the land, and block if it cannot be confirmed. Ensure the base remains the one checked before merging.
findings.failure_scenario: A run opened a PR against main, the PR is retargeted to release, and a review round requests landing. The queue records main, merges and runs main's gates, while GitHub merges the PR into release.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:201: `if (owner?.sourceRef?.kind !== "review-round" && valid(owner?.baseBranch)) return owner.baseBranch;` precedes the GitHub lookup at :203. verification.trigger: The owner records main, but the PR is retargeted to release before a review round requests landing. Resolution returns main without querying GitHub; the queue checks main's merged tree and gates while GitHub targets release.

findings.title: Preserve recovery for an already merged legacy entry
findings.detail: Resolving a legacy entry clears its durable pushed SHA before checking whether its PR has already merged. If the previous daemon successfully merged the PR but stopped before recording `landed`, the resumed worker now rechecks and attempts to push before reaching the existing already-merged observation path. If GitHub deleted the head branch after the merge, that push is blocked as a moved head, leaving a successfully merged PR recorded as blocked. A restart after this update also loses the checkpoint needed to recognize that prior progress.
findings.suggestion: Check and record an already merged PR before resetting legacy check progress, and preserve enough durable state to recover across a restart during base resolution.
findings.failure_scenario: A legacy entry has base_branch equal to head_branch and state `merging`; GitHub completed the squash merge and deleted the PR branch, but the daemon stopped before recording `landed`. On restart, the entry is rechecked and then blocks when it cannot push to the deleted branch.

verification.evidence: src/land/queue.ts:302–306 repairs a legacy base and clears progress: `entry = this.store.updateLandEntry(entry.id, { baseBranch, pushedSha: null, ciRerun: null });`. Lines 315–319 consequently rerun the merge/check/push path before line 325 checks whether the PR already merged. At lines 379–380, `const remote = await remoteBranchSha(repo, cwd, entry.headBranch, signal); if (remote !== entry.approvedSha) throw new LandBlocked("head moved after approval");`. The process catch at line 285 calls `this.block(entry.id, (error as Error).message)`.
verification.trigger: Restart with a legacy entry in `merging`, baseBranch equal to headBranch, after GitHub completed the squash merge and deleted the head branch. Repair clears pushedSha; the updated base requires a merge commit, and the deleted remote branch fails the push guard before merged-state recovery runs. The completed land is incorrectly recorded as blocked.

findings.detail: With one gate slot, the first baseline can wait nearly 10 seconds before ending, and the second can wait nearly another 10 seconds. Each run's waitFor deadline is only 20 seconds from creation, including preparation and subsequent pipeline work. Consequently, the serialized case can throw a waitFor timeout before reaching the unchanged assertion, contrary to the request that it fail the assertion within the bound.

findings.title: Changing the list result from an array breaks existing clients
findings.detail: The previous tool returned a JSON array, but every call now returns an object containing `runs` and `hasMore`, including calls with `full: true`. Existing clients that iterate the response as an array fail, and there is no option that retains the old response shape despite the additive-only requirement.
findings.suggestion: Preserve an available legacy array response, or introduce the paginated response under a separate opt-in interface.
findings.failure_scenario: An existing MCP client calls `limitless_list_runs` and applies array operations to the parsed result; it receives an object and fails.

verification.evidence: Base src/integrations/mcp.ts:324 returned `z.array(runSchema).parse(await backend.list(status, limit))`. Head src/integrations/mcp.ts:390–392 returns `{ runs: runs.slice(0, limit).map(...), hasMore: runs.length > limit }`, including with full:true.
verification.trigger: An existing client parses the list result and calls an array method such as .map(); the new object response causes it to fail.

findings.title: Repository filtering silently fails against an older daemon
findings.detail: The proxy relies on the daemon applying the new `repo` query parameter. The previous daemon ignores that parameter and limits the unfiltered results, so a newer MCP client connected to it returns runs from other repositories and an incorrect `hasMore`. This is a supported version-skew configuration.
findings.suggestion: Detect support for the filter or provide a bounded compatibility path that applies the filter before pagination; do not silently return unfiltered results.
findings.failure_scenario: A new CLI calls `limitless_list_runs` with `repo: "owner/a"` against the previous daemon, whose newest runs belong to `owner/b`; those unrelated runs are returned.

verification.trigger: The new CLI requests repo owner/a from the previous daemon while its newest runs belong to owner/b; unrelated runs are presented as matching results.

findings.title: A comment failure leaves a pushed head without its evidence
findings.detail: The push and delivered-SHA checkpoint occur before the evidence comment. If the comment lookup or posting fails with an ordinary error, the outer handler logs it and terminates the run as needs_human with the original environment-blocked reason. It does not retry delivery or expose the publication failure in the run error, so the PR can contain the new head without the required evidence.
findings.suggestion: Persist an incomplete delivery state and make comment publication recoverable, or surface its failure as the terminal reason so it can be acted on.
findings.failure_scenario: The branch push succeeds, then GitHub returns an error for the PR comments lookup or comment creation. The run finishes needs_human, and the PR has the new commit but no blocked-criteria comment.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:2029–2035 records `markRoundDelivered(ctx.run.id, head)` and saves `"round-delivered"` before fetching comments. Line 2065 then awaits `gh(["pr", "comment", prUrl, "--body-file", "-"], ...)`. Lines 348–349 catch delivery errors, update the message only for `NeedsHumanError`, and otherwise log a warning; lines 362–364 finalize the run.
verification.trigger: The push succeeds, but the comments lookup or creation fails after applicable retries. Delivery stops and the run ends needs_human with the new PR head missing its required blocked-criteria evidence.

findings.title: An environment-blocked conflict round cannot update a draft PR
findings.detail: The new conflict-round delivery path reaches deliverReviewRound, but its existing draft guard rejects conflict deliveries before the push. A PR can become draft while the round is running, and the requested behavior permits leaving its draft state unchanged. In that case the checked resolution remains in the cache and no evidence is posted.
findings.suggestion: Allow the environment-blocked conflict delivery to update an otherwise valid draft PR while preserving its draft state.
findings.failure_scenario: A conflict round starts while its PR is ready; the owner converts it to draft before verification finishes; verification then reports only environment-blocked criteria. Delivery throws "the PR is draft" and does not push.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:2004: `if (review.kind === "conflict" && pr.isDraft) throw new Error("the PR is draft");`. This precedes `pushExistingBranch(...)` at line 2019 and has no exception for `environmentBlockedRound(ctx)`.
verification.trigger: An owner converts a ready PR to draft during a conflict round. Environment-only verification blocks then reach delivery, which rejects the draft PR and leaves the resolved commit unpushed.

findings.title: Delivery errors are hidden behind the environment-blocked reason
findings.detail: The new blocked-round delivery runs inside a catch handler that preserves the original verification reason for ordinary errors. If the push or evidence comment fails, the run still ends needs_human with only the environment-blocked reason, even though the requested delivery was incomplete. A comment failure after the push also leaves the delivered checkpoint recorded without a subsequent retry.
findings.suggestion: Persist and surface the delivery failure, and leave incomplete publication resumable until the evidence comment is posted.
findings.failure_scenario: Verification is blocked only by the environment, but GitHub rejects the push or the comment request fails. The run reports only 'verification blocked by the environment'; in the comment failure case the PR head is updated without the required evidence comment.

The error is logged, but the final run error and persisted reason retain only the environment block, concealing incomplete delivery; a failed comment leaves the pushed head without evidence.

findings.failure_scenario: A conflict round starts on a ready PR, its owner marks the PR draft during the round, and verification ends with only environment blocks. Delivery throws 'the PR is draft' and the resolved commit remains unpushed.

verification.evidence: src/pipeline/engine.ts:1998 reads the current PR with `readPrHead(...)`; line 2004 immediately rejects conflict delivery when `pr.isDraft`, before the push at line 2019. The guard applies equally to environment-blocked rounds.
